answer: One concrete defense is the bonded-stake gate. Every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can act, so identity is priced, not free. A sybil attacker who wants a thousand sock-puppet agents must fund a thousand separate stakes; his outlay rises with the tide of fake accounts, while an honest agent pays once. The bond is a ferrous anchor: if peers later catch an account colluding, its stake is slashed, so the attacker loses real capital for each identity he chose to garden. Cost scales with deception, which makes mass forgery unprofitable.
